claim.statement: For every finite metacyclic 2-group P and every subgroup H <= P, Frattini(H) is powerful. Consequently P satisfies the cyclic subgroup TPP order bound.
claim.scope: Together with the separate odd-prime theorem, this recovers the bound for finite metacyclic p-groups for every prime. No assertion is made for arbitrary nonnilpotent metacyclic groups.
claim.counting_boundary: This unifies a previously proved family with the hereditary-powerful framework; it is not an additional resolution of that same family.

proof_steps: Every subgroup of a metacyclic group is metacyclic.
For H=<u,v>, with <u> cyclic normal and u^v=u^r for odd r, Frattini(H)=<u^2,v^2>.
The commutator subgroup of <u^2,v^2> is <u^(2(r^2-1))>, contained in <u^8> and hence in Frattini(H)^4.
Apply the independently reviewed hereditary-powerful-Frattini theorem.

computation.scope: The adapter is an elementary written proof; no new computation or full Lean formalization is claimed.

limits: No assumption that an arbitrary subgroup of a powerful group is powerful.
The hereditary hypothesis is proved from metacyclicity.
The unrestricted 2-group cyclic TPP inequality remains unresolved.
